title: Modality II (v0.52.0)
description: Modality II in Soup CLI v0.52.0 (live trainers v0.53.2 + PRM live v0.53.11). task: tts with 5 family names (Orpheus, Sesame-CSM, Llasa, Spark, Oute) + emotion vocab; at v0.77.0 all five are runnable: spark and oute only on pre-encoded chatml data, and sesame_csm on raw audio through a native trainer (refused at config load in v0.76.x). task: classifier/reranker/cross_encoder live. task: distill live with teacher_model + KL/JS divergence + temperature. task: prm live with per-step MSE. BitNet 1.58 quant (refused at config load since v0.76.0 because BitNet training is not implemented; GGUF export is live). EBFT + GDPO variants (refused at config load since v0.76.0). MoE expert quant. reasoning_effort dispatch.

blocks.html:
Modality II (v0.52.0)

7 parts. New task families + BitNet + EBFT/GDPO + MoE quant. +237 tests (6968 → 7205).

Since v0.76.0: quantization: bitnet_1.58, ebft_variant and gdpo_variant are refused at config load, and data.format: audio is refused for the spark and oute families. tts_family: sesame_csm was refused through v0.76.x and trains through a native trainer since v0.77.0 (#1769). The sections below are kept as the record of what v0.52.0 shipped and now say what is true at v0.77.0.

TTS (task: tts)

Five tts_family values with per-family emotion vocabularies, all runnable at v0.77.0: orpheus and llasa on raw audio or pre-encoded data, spark and oute on pre-encoded data only (see below), and sesame_csm on raw audio through its own trainer (see Native Sesame CSM). Through v0.76.x sesame_csm was refused at config load.

blocks.code:
task: tts
modality: audio_out
base: canopylabs/orpheus-3b-0.1-ft
data:
  format: audio
  train: ./data/tts.jsonl
training:
  tts_family: orpheus   # orpheus | llasa | spark | oute | sesame_csm (its own settings, below)
  tts_emotion: happy    # a single string, not a list

blocks.html:
Cross-validator gates per family. canopylabs/orpheus requires tts_family: orpheus.

Only two families take an emotion tag, and each has its own list. Orpheus accepts neutral, happy, sad, angry, excited, calm, whisper and laugh; Oute accepts neutral, happy, sad, angry, calm and excited. Llasa, Spark and Sesame-CSM refuse tts_emotion outright (tts_family='llasa' does not support emotion conditioning), and a tag outside a family's list is refused when the config loads (laugh on oute, for instance). For the two families that take one, the trainer prepends a family-specific control string to the first user turn of every row: <|emotion|>happy<|/emotion|> for Orpheus and [emotion: happy] for Oute.

data.format: audio encodes raw audio at train time, and what it needs depends on the family.

  • Orpheus (pip install snac, 24 kHz) and Llasa (Soup's [audio] extra: torchaudio and soundfile; torchaudio must match the installed Torch; audio is resampled to 16 kHz and encoded with HKUSTAudio/xcodec2-hf, the ids rendered as <|s_ID|>) are live on this path.
  • Spark and Oute raw-audio configs are refused at config load, with the compatibility reason: Spark-TTS has no installable sparktts package and its official environment pins Torch and Transformers below Soup's stack, and the current outetts pins Transformers 4.52.3 (Oute also needs transcript or word alignment). Through v0.75.2 these were described as raising a runtime error naming a missing package.
  • sesame_csm takes raw audio only, through a native trainer rather than this codec-string path (since v0.77.0, see below). A pre-encoded chatml config is refused, because CSM trains text plus 32 Mimi codebooks as parallel frames, which is not a codec-token chat. Through v0.76.x it was refused whatever the data format. The sesame-csm-tts and spark-tts recipes removed in v0.76.0 have not come back.

The path that runs everywhere is the pre-encoded one: encode your audio to codec tokens yourself (in the upstream codec's own environment, for Spark and Oute), register them through data.new_special_tokens, and train with data.format: chatml (or auto) over the token text, as rows with a messages list. data.new_special_tokens is registered on backend: transformers only; backend: unsloth with it is refused at load (#1358). chat is not a value of data.format, even though Soup's own error message for a missing codec package says it is. Three TTS recipes ship: orpheus-tts-sft and llasa-tts (raw audio, data.format: audio) and oute-tts (pre-encoded, data.format: chatml).

Native Sesame CSM (v0.77.0)

tts_family: sesame_csm trains with Transformers' own CsmForConditionalGeneration and CsmProcessor (#1769, by @Amix29). Upstream describes the objective this way: the processor builds the text conditioning and the audio-frame labels, the model encodes each clip with its frozen Mimi codec, and the loss is the sum of the backbone's loss on the first codebook and the depth decoder's on the other 31. Install the audio extra beside training:
Each JSONL row is one local clip and its exact transcript, with role set to the speaker id, "0" or "1":

blocks.code:
base: sesame/csm-1b
backend: transformers
task: tts
modality: audio_out
data:
  train: ./data/speech.jsonl
  format: audio
  audio_dir: ./data/audio
  max_length: 2048
training:
  tts_family: sesame_csm
  quantization: none      # required: the schema default, 4bit, is refused
  epochs: 3
  batch_size: 1
  gradient_accumulation_steps: 4
  lr: 0.00002
  lora:
    r: 16
    alpha: 32

blocks.html:
LoRA goes on the backbone and the depth decoder, never on Mimi; lora.r: 0 is full fine-tuning, with Mimi still frozen. What it refuses, at config load unless noted:

  • A data.format other than audio, a backend other than transformers, and any training.quantization but none. Leaving quantization out is refused too, because its default is 4bit: Sesame CSM requires training.quantization='none'.
  • Every training setting outside this list when it differs from its default: epochs, lr, batch_size, gradient_accumulation_steps, seed, data_seed, warmup_ratio, weight_decay, max_grad_norm, optimizer, scheduler, save_steps, logging_steps, eval_steps and a boolean gradient_checkpointing; under lora everything but r, alpha and dropout; under data everything but train, format, val_split, max_length and audio_dir. The message names the setting, for example Sesame CSM does not support training.packing. tts_emotion is one of them.
  • A row that is not one clip with exactly one transcript message, or whose role is not "0" or "1": checked after the data loads and before the model does, naming the split and the row. soup train --dry-run runs this check too.
  • More than one device, a distributed launch, DeepSpeed or FSDP, when the trainer is set up (on a multi-GPU box, select one card with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES).
  • A sequence longer than data.max_length, when its batch is built: it is refused rather than truncated, because cutting the audio markers would break the codec alignment.

batch_size: auto uses 1. Validation loss, seeds, resume and saving the processor are supported. Audio is read through Soup's local-file checks and resampled to mono 24 kHz. sesame/csm-1b may need Hugging Face access; a local Transformers-format CSM checkpoint works too.

What was checked, and what was not. Upstream's offline tests build a tiny CSM model with all 32 Mimi codebooks and exercise forward and backward, training, evaluation, save and reload, and resume, and one LoRA step on a tiny random CSM model also ran on Apple Silicon (MPS). Upstream says that validates the integration and does not establish speech quality, and no full training run on the pretrained sesame/csm-1b checkpoint is recorded. No quality or speed figure is published here. Raw-audio Spark and Oute are unchanged: still pre-encoded only.

Distillation (task: distill)

blocks.code:
task: distill
base: meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B
training:
  teacher_model: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct
  distill_divergence: kl         # kl | forward_kl | reverse_kl | js
  distill_temperature: 2.0       # [0.05, 100]

blocks.html:
kl is an alias for forward_kl, which is also what an unset distill_divergence resolves to; an unset distill_temperature resolves to 2.0. Distillation runs on backend: transformers only (mlx and unsloth are refused at config load), and on modality: text only: since v0.77.0 vision and audio are refused at load, because the trainer loads a text-only student and teacher (#2014; through v0.76.1 they were accepted and ignored). It loads the student unquantized: an unset quantization resolves to none, and since v0.77.0 an explicit quantization: 4bit or 8bit (or load_in_8bit: true) stops the load with has no effect on task='distill' (see Keys a task ignores). training.gradient_checkpointing: true reaches the distill trainer since v0.77.0; it used to train with checkpointing off whatever the key said. Every train and validation row must keep at least one causal-loss target after truncation at data.max_length, or the run is refused at setup naming the split and row. distill_mode: sequence (the teacher generates a completion per prompt and the student trains with plain cross-entropy on it, instead of matching logits) cannot be combined with uld_strategy or minillm_enabled: the schema accepts the pair, and the distill trainer refuses it at setup, before any model loads. In sequence mode a row with no prompt turn is skipped, with the count and first positions printed.

Memory controls (v0.76.0)

Distillation with a large vocabulary and long sequences can run out of GPU memory on the logit and probability tensors the divergence builds. Two keys bound it:

blocks.code:
task: distill
training:
  teacher_model: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct
  distill_chunk_size: 256     # evaluate the divergence over chunks of response tokens
  distill_checkpoint: true    # recompute each chunk in backward instead of storing it

blocks.html:
distill_chunk_size (an integer of at least 1) evaluates the divergence over chunks of response tokens, which bounds the transient peak. distill_checkpoint wraps each chunk in non-reentrant activation checkpointing, which cuts the bytes held for backward at the cost of recomputation. distill_checkpoint without distill_chunk_size treats all response tokens as one chunk: it reduces what is retained and leaves the transient peak unbounded. Both are refused outside task: distill, and with uld_strategy, minillm_enabled or distill_mode: sequence. No memory figure is published for them.

Two numerics changes ride with it. The three divergences are now evaluated in FP32 and the loss scalar is FP32, so values differ slightly from the old low-precision numbers. Gradient accumulation weights by the number of shifted, non-masked targets across the whole optimizer window, so splitting the same rows into unequal-length microbatches keeps the full-batch token mean. Cross-tokenizer uld_strategy: wasserstein_aligned now leaves out a student token with no teacher counterpart (#1426); re-run a distillation whose tokenizers differ in byte-fallback or special tokens.

Classifier / Reranker / Cross-Encoder

blocks.code:
task: classifier   # | reranker | cross_encoder
training:
  num_labels: 5
  label_names: ["very_bad", "bad", "neutral", "good", "very_good"]
  classifier_kind: single_label   # or multi_label (v0.52.0)
  classifier_lora: false          # true wraps the head with LoRA (v0.71.12)

blocks.html:
Row shapes: classifier takes {"text": "...", "label": 1} or a label name, and for multi_label a list of active indices or names ({"text": "...", "label": [0, 2]}); reranker takes {"text": "query doc", "label": ...}; cross_encoder takes {"text_a": "query", "text_b": "doc", "label": 1} or {"question": "query", "answer": "doc", "label": 1} and, for task: cross_encoder, data.format: auto (the default) reads that pair shape; the explicit value data.format: cross_encoder (v0.76.0) is accepted only on that task and is refused on any other. These three tasks load the base unquantized, and since v0.77.0 an explicit quantization: 4bit or 8bit stops the load. training.gradient_checkpointing: true reaches them since v0.77.0 (their default stays off).

classifier_kind picks the head: single_label is the default for task: classifier, multi_label trains one independent decision per label rather than a choice between them. classifier_lora is opt-in: it wraps the sequence-classification head as a PEFT SEQ_CLS adapter instead of full fine-tuning, and the ordinary training.lora block still supplies r / alpha / dropout when you turn it on.

BitNet 1.58-bit (schema and export only)

training.quantization: bitnet_1.58 is refused at config load on every task and backend (v0.76.0): BitNet 1.58 training is not implemented yet; the export path soup export --format tq1_0 works on an existing BitNet checkpoint. Through v0.75.2 the schema accepted the value and the quantization loader then rejected it after the config had validated; the BitNetTrainerWrapper that was meant to take over had no caller in soup train. The falcon-e-bitnet-sft recipe set this key and was removed from the catalog in v0.76.0.

The export side is separate and is wired: soup export --format bitnet or tq1_0 runs llama.cpp's converter and then llama-quantize with the TQ1_0 type (it needs a built llama.cpp). is_bitnet_model is a name heuristic that matches a few prefixes (bitnet, falcon-e, falcone, 1bitllm, onebit), not a check of the weights.

EBFT + GDPO variants (refused since v0.76.0)

Both fields are refused at config load, in every value.

  • training.gdpo_variant (standard, length_normalized, margin) is refused (#1309): supported TRL versions (0.29 and later) no longer expose the DPO loss hook it depended on, so on those versions it was accepted and silently trained plain DPO. Remove it. Plain task: dpo is what standard ran; task: simpo is the nearest, not identical, length-normalised objective for length_normalized; margin has no equivalent.
  • training.ebft_variant (structured, strided) and training.ebft_temperature are refused (#1230): the term scored each position's logits against that position's own input token with no causal shift, so it rewarded copying the input; shifted onto the next token it duplicates the model's cross-entropy. ebft_temperature on its own is refused too.

No shipped recipe, template or example sets either field. The kernels this page described as live from v0.53.2 are not reachable from a config.

MoE expert quant

blocks.code:
training:
  moe_lora: true                 # required: moe_expert_quant is refused without it
  moe_expert_quant: nf4          # nf4 | int8_rowwise
  train_router_only: true        # freeze experts, train router only

blocks.html:
moe_expert_quant and train_router_only are read by task: sft and tts only and are refused at load on any other task. moe_expert_quant quantizes experts that are one nn.Linear each, and it needs CUDA and bitsandbytes. On a transformers 5 fused-expert MoE (Qwen3-30B-A3B is one) the experts are fused 3-D tensors with no nn.Linear to quantize, so the setup refuses with the architecture and the fused parameters named; through v0.75.2 it printed applied to 0 expert Linear block(s) and trained in full precision. moe_lora still adapts those experts, with lora.dropout: 0.0; see Backends.

Reasoning effort dispatch

blocks.code:
training:
  reasoning_effort: medium       # low | medium | high  (gpt-oss family)
  train_on_eot: true             # also train on the end-of-turn token

blocks.html:
Both keys are applied by the SFT formatter, so since v0.77.0 (#806, #1587) they load only on sft, tts (which trains through the SFT trainer) and distill: on any other task the config fails with training.reasoning_effort='high' requires task in ['distill', 'sft', 'tts']; got task='pretrain'. Through v0.76.1 they were refused on tts, where they apply, and accepted on pretrain, classifier, reranker and cross_encoder, which never read them; removing them from such a config changes nothing about what trains. On pretrain, train_on_eot changed only the soup data preprocess cache key, so a pretrain cache built with the flag has to be rebuilt without it. reasoning_effort prepends <|reasoning_effort|>medium<|/reasoning_effort|> to the first system message of every row, and inserts a system message at the top when the row has none. train_on_eot extends the assistant-only loss mask to include the end-of-turn token that follows each assistant reply, so the model is trained to emit the terminator; it acts through the assistant-only masking path, which is on by default (data.train_on_responses_only: true), and with that turned off it has nothing to extend.

v0.52.0 shipped the schema; v0.53.2 lit up the trainers — task: distill (DistillTrainerWrapper with KL/forward_kl/reverse_kl/js), task: classifier | reranker | cross_encoder (single-label / multi-label / cross-encoder heads), EBFT + GDPO loss kernels, and reasoning_effort dispatch. (Since closed in v0.76.0: the EBFT and GDPO fields are refused at config load, as above.) See v0.53.2 — Modality II live.
